column1: # CANONICAL HEARTBEAT CHECKER REGISTRY
# This file is the SINGLE source of truth for which checkers belong to the
# recurring heartbeat pass. The runner (ops/run-heartbeat-checks.py) reads it,
# and ops/test-heartbeat-registry.py enforces it.
# WHY A REGISTRY: the orphaned-publisher bug (2026-10-26) was structural.
# `blotato-fallback.js` had no cron, no checklist entry, and nothing invoked
# it - so it did nothing for days. Later the SAME shape was found again:
# `ops/dead-inbox-check.py` was a working, tested checker that HEARTBEAT.md
# named NOWHERE. A checker on disk that no pass runs is a comment, not a
# control. So: every checker file in ops/ MUST appear below, classified as
# PASS (runs every pass) or SCOPE (deliberately not recurring, with a reason).
# A new checker that nobody classified FAILS the suite. That is the point.
# COLUMNS (pipe-separated, one checker per line):
#   name      | short id used in the runner's summary
#   path      | path relative to the repo root
#   scope     | PASS = runs every heartbeat pass
#              | SCOPE = deliberately not recurring (a reason is REQUIRED)
#   contract  | exit codes: 0=clean, 1=finding, 2=could-not-prove, - = n/a
#   known     | yes = a non-zero here is an ALREADY-ESCALATED condition
#   purpose   | one line: what this checker actually checks
#   reason    | required when scope=SCOPE; blank otherwise
# name | path | scope | contract | known | purpose | reason
drift | ops/drift-check.py | PASS | 0,1,2 | no | live pages vs the registry that owns them |
price-on-feed | ops/check-price-on-feed.py | PASS | 0,1,2 | yes | rule [10]: no price on a public feed |

caviar-on-feed | ops/check-caviar-on-feed.py | PASS | 0,1,2 | yes | a live public post that offers caviar | 2026-10-30: a retail Oscietra caviar offer went live on Threads (8676561 / DfG_M2bEd5U) with NO price in the caption, so the price guard could not see it and no checker looked at the product at all. This checker audits the LIVE feed for a caviar offer; on its first run it found THREE live posts, not one (also IG 8634450 'Take our caviar import...' and IG 8592075 'Caviar imported and distributed... priced per 100g'). It is a KNOWN escalation because the remedy is a human deleting a post and Blotato has no delete route. It scans ONLY the accounts we own: this key also carries laisa_aesthetics (55765), and a check whose remedy is a deletion must never flag another brand's post |
staged-publish | ops/check-staged-publish.py | PASS | 0,1,- | yes | staged captions that never reached any platform |
cost-model | ops/check-cost-model-exposure.py | PASS | 0,1,2 | yes | a public page leaking our cost model |
tmp-surface | ops/tmp-shape-surface-audit.py | PASS | 0,3,- | no | credential literals under /tmp |
credential-slots | ops/check-credential-slots.py | PASS | 0,1,- | no | a credential slot that holds a placeholder instead of a credential |
tracked-creds | ops/check-tracked-live-credentials.py | PASS | 0,1,- | no | live credential literals in tracked files |
dead-inbox | ops/dead-inbox-check.py | PASS | 0,1,- | no | code referencing a mailbox nobody can read |
mail | ops/check-latest-mail.py | PASS | 0,-,2 | no | newest inbound AgentMail message |
scanner-log | ops/check-scanner-log-exposure.py | PASS | 0,1,- | no | live credential literals in the gateway log, the cron run history, the session transcripts AND the agent's memory database |
cron-payload-claims | ops/check-cron-payload-claims.py | PASS | 0,1,- | no | no cron payload hardcodes a system-status claim |
cron-times | ops/check-cron-times.py | PASS | 0,1,- | no | every cron job fires when its own name promises |

cron-timeouts | ops/check-cron-timeout-outliers.py | PASS | 0,1,- | no | a cron job budgeted far below its own siblings - a budget too small for the work silently kills the job | 2026-10-29: ceo-standup-0900 carried 300s where its own family carried 1800s, so it was killed 3.5 seconds past the line with an empty summary and deliveryStatus "unknown" - Tumelo simply did not get his standup, and nothing said so. The 22 Oct round that raised the fleet's timeouts never included this job. A SHORT timeout is legitimate; an OUTLIER one is not, so the rule is relative to the job's own name family

cron-kills | ops/check-cron-timeout-kills.py | PASS | 0,1,2 | no | a cron job whose last run was killed by a timeout its CURRENT budget could not have avoided | the pass could see a MIS-BUDGETED job but not a DEAD one: no checker read the run records, so the 09:00 standup's kill sat unread for a day. The rule compares the kill against the CURRENT budget, so a job that has already been repaired is not re-announced as a defect until its next run proves it - a guard that cries wolf gets switched off

pass-completion | ops/check-pass-completion.py | PASS | 0,1,2 | no | a scheduled pass slot that produced NO completed pass - the guards were silent, not green | on 2026-10-30 the 03:23Z and 04:23Z pass slots never ran: both cron turns died of an upstream API rate limit before the runner was invoked, so no log, no state key, no note and no Discord message existed. Neither cron-times (the job fired on time) nor cron-kills (the run was not killed by a timeout) could see it, and no other checker reads whether THE PASS ITSELF ran. The rule asks one question per slot - is there evidence the runner reached its VERDICT line? - and a slot that is still owed but produced nothing is a finding. The window is short so a two-hour-old gap ages out instead of being re-announced for ever

spec-traceability | ops/check-spec-traceability.py | PASS | 0,1,2 | no | a numeric QUALITY claim (marbling grade, marble score) in the content catalog that its owning source does not support | 2026-10-30: the caption machine published 'marbling grade 5' about the Wagyu Ribeye (Threads 8633885) - it did NOT invent it, it copied the content catalog's own tagline, while the owning source (studex-products-catalog.csv) says 'marble scores 8+ to 11+'. (CORRECTED 2026-10-31: this reason originally also named IG 8634450; that post is the enterprise lead-time caption and carries no marble claim - the ribeye caption went to Threads only.) The price guard compares CURRENCY and can never see a quality tier, so the whole class was unguarded. The rule is PER-PRODUCT: the owning source legitimately contains '5-7 marble score' and 'Marble Score 7/8' for other products, so a corpus-wide check would wave 'grade 5' through
client-secret | ops/check-client-secret-exposure.py | PASS | 0,1,- | no | a browser bundle can hold a secret |
leak-sources | ops/check-leak-sources.py | PASS | 0,1,- | no | which files and scripts can still leak a credential value |
discord-credential | ops/check-discord-credential-exposure.py | PASS | 0,1,2 | no | a live credential literal in a Discord message we posted |
public-exposure | ops/check-public-exposure.py | PASS | 0,1,2 | yes | a credential that still authenticates is reachable from the public remote |

blotato-placement | ops/check-blotato-placement.py | SCOPE | 0,-,- | no | one-off diagnostic: where the live Blotato key lives on disk | forensic, not a standing condition - run it when investigating a Blotato finding, not every pass
catalog | ops/check-catalog.py | SCOPE | 0,-,- | no | one-off content-catalog audit plus a Perplexity probe | audits a specific catalog state that only changes on a deliberate rebuild
content-agent | ops/check-content-agent.py | SCOPE | 0,-,- | no | one-off LLM-provider probe and timeout tuning for the content agent | a repair tool for a specific incident, not a standing control

probe-ads-performance | ops/probe-ads-performance.py | SCOPE | 0,-,- | no | a read-only Meta Ads spend / impressions / actions probe | a one-off diagnostic for one question (Meta's graph token expired on 27 Jun, so the probe reports the expiry rather than a standing condition); it reads the token in-process and every call is a GET

probe-eod-storefront | ops/probe-eod-storefront-2026-10-30.py | SCOPE | 0,-,- | no | a read-only end-of-day storefront and content-metrics probe | a dated one-off (2026-10-30) that answered three questions once - is the buying path alive, what does the live price ladder say, do today's posts carry metrics yet; not a recurring control

surfaced-candidates | ops/check-surfaced-candidates.py | SCOPE | 0,-,- | no | checks three specific credential-shaped candidates from one scan | the candidates are a closed set from a past scan; resolving them is a project, not a check
surfaced-candidates-live | ops/check-surfaced-candidates-live.py | SCOPE | 0,-,- | no | liveness-probes two remaining surfaced candidates | a one-time liveness resolution of a closed set
pre-push-guard | ops/check-pre-push-guard.py | PASS | 0,1,2 | no | the pre-push guard that stops a live credential being published to the public repo is installed and matches its source |

git-index | ops/check-git-index.py | PASS | 0,1,2 | no | the git index is intact and consistent with HEAD - an emptied index makes every tracked file look staged for deletion, and a GITLINK (mode 160000) makes a clone carry an empty directory that no content-based checker can see | 2026-10-29: a leftover scratch dir from ops/test-empty-repo-false-green.py held its own .git repos and .gitignore only covered .tmp-*.sh/.tmp-*.py - FILES, not DIRECTORIES - so `git add .` would have staged them as embedded repos and shipped gitlinks to a PUBLIC remote. The index was consistent with HEAD, so every other check stayed green. The guard now reads git's own record of the index entry by entry, including the mode

credential-fragments | ops/audit-credential-fragments.py | PASS | 0,1 | yes | a fragment of ANY live credential sits in tracked source | it REPLACES ops/audit-blotato-fragments.py, which watched ONE credential out of fifty and reported CLEAN while 22 tracked files held fragments of 15 credentials - 7 of them proven LIVE. The scope was the defect, not the bug: a guard that watches one key while the repo holds fifty is a guard for a key nobody else has. Known escalation because the full keys are already published in the public remote - ROTATION is the fix and only Tumelo can rotate a credential

cred-resolution | ops/credential-resolution-check.py | PASS | 0,1,- | no | a credential reference in tracked source that does not resolve, or a hardcoded credential | the language-aware SHAPE checker, complementary to check-tracked-live-credentials.py which asks the VALUE question. The 2026-10-24 incident was exactly the case where the shape checker said CLEAN over 4202 files holding 10 live credentials, so the value checker was added - running only one of the pair is how it happened

preflight-daily-post | ops/preflight-daily-post.py | SCOPE | 0,1,- | no | the 09:00 publish and the path-B fallback caption | it is the GATE, not a checker: the 08:00 and 09:20 crons run it via scripts/preflight-cron.sh and its cron instruction is "if it exits 0, do NOTHING". It is deliberately outside the pass because the pass must not post to Discord

git-pre-push-hook | ops/git-pre-push-guard.py | SCOPE | 0,1,- | no | blocks a push that would expose a credential | it is invoked by GIT as a pre-push hook, not by the pass - git is its runner. The suite exercises it via ops/test-git-pre-push-guard.py

memory-shrink-guard | ops/memory-shrink-guard.py | SCOPE | 0,1,- | no | a long-term memory file silently loses a committed section | a guard the SUITE runs (ops/run-tests.sh), not a pass checker; it needs a stable git index, which the pass does not guarantee
eod-blotato | ops/eod-blotato-check.py | SCOPE | 0,1,2 | yes | end-of-day Blotato state | a one-off end-of-day diagnostic on its own schedule
probe-blotato-posts | ops/probe-blotato-posts.py | SCOPE | 0,1,2 | no | read-only listing of published Blotato posts | an ad-hoc read-only probe, run by hand when a post needs to be located
probe-live-bundles | ops/probe-live-bundles.py | SCOPE | 0,1,2 | no | read-only listing of live bundles | an ad-hoc read-only probe
probe-providers | ops/probe-providers.py | SCOPE | 0,1,2 | no | which LLM providers answer | a one-off provider probe from 2026-08; superseded by ops/check-content-agent.py
probe-providers2 | ops/probe-providers2.py | SCOPE | 0,1,2 | no | which LLM providers answer (second pass) | a one-off provider probe from 2026-08; superseded by ops/check-content-agent.py
probe-shopify-admin | ops/probe-shopify-admin.py | SCOPE | 0,1,2 | no | read-only Shopify Admin check | an ad-hoc read-only probe used when a storefront price is in doubt

heartbeat-legacy | ops/heartbeat-check.py | SCOPE | 0,1,2 | no | the pre-registry consolidated heartbeat check | SUPERSEDED by ops/run-heartbeat-checks.py, which is the canonical pass; kept for history only

patch-correction-scan | ops/patch-correction-scan.py | SCOPE | 0,1,2 | no | scans a correction patch for unapplied changes | a one-off patch audit; not a control because it only means something against one specific patch

patch-draft-scan | ops/patch-draft-scan.py | SCOPE | 0,1,2 | no | scans a draft patch for unapplied changes | a one-off patch audit; not a control because it only means something against one specific patch

secret-leak-scan | ops/secret_leak_scan.py | SCOPE | 0,1,2 | no | credential-shaped literals in browser-served assets | it is a LIBRARY imported by ops/drift-check.py, which runs it as the "Secret leak scan" step - it has no standalone entry point of its own

price-ladder | ops/price-ladder-guard.py | SCOPE | 0,-,- | no | price-ladder inversion + caviar-compliance audit across the live pages | it runs in the BUILD HOUR (builds/2026-10-28.md step 4), not in the pass: it reports catalogue and Shopify price questions only the owner can answer, and it must see the day's final deploys rather than run all day

git-pre-commit-hook | ops/git-pre-commit-guard.py | SCOPE | 0,1,- | no | blocks a commit that would expose a credential into the PUBLIC remote | it is invoked by GIT as a pre-commit hook - git is its runner, not the pass; ops/check-pre-push-guard.py verifies the installed .githooks/pre-commit copy matches this source

cta-on-feed | ops/check-cta-on-feed.py | PASS | 0,1,2 | yes | a live public post with no call to action | 2026-10-31: the feed reached people and asked for nothing. Measured on the LIVE feed (Blotato /posts -> state.analytics.latest.metrics), 10 posts: Instagram 5/5 carry a CTA ('Connect with our team: info@studexmeat.com'), 1060-1239 chars, never truncated; Threads 0/5 carry one, every one exactly 500 chars (TRUNCATED). Threads 3 likes vs Instagram 47; EVERY post 0 comments, 0 follows, 0 shares; best post 841 views / 489 reach / 5 profile visits / 0 follows. ROOT CAUSE was a truncation, not a strategy: both publish paths cut Threads at 497 chars and the CTA lives at the END of a caption, so the cut deleted exactly the CTA - and the generator's validator ('no closing question/CTA') had already APPROVED the pre-truncation text. FIXED in scripts/caption_policy.py (truncate_for_platform cuts the PROSE, keeps the CTA + hashtags). This checker audits the LIVE feed for the posts that are already CTA-less. It is a KNOWN escalation because the remedy is a human editing a post and Blotato has no edit route. It scans ONLY the accounts we own (this key also carries laisa_aesthetics (55765), and a check whose remedy is an edit must never flag another brand's post) |

cron-count-claims | ops/check-cron-count-claims.py | PASS | 0,1,2 | no | a cron payload that states a checker count the registry contradicts | 2026-10-31: registering cta-on-feed as the 26th checker left the canonical pass's payload saying 'It is 25 READ-ONLY checkers' - the pass would run 26 while its own instructions said 25. NOTHING CAUGHT IT: the registry test checks that every checker on disk is classified and every registered checker EXISTS (neither is 'does the payload's number match'), and check-cron-payload-claims checks for a FALSE STATUS (a stale number is not a false status). This checker derives the count from the registry's PASS rows and compares it to any count a payload STATES - it is silent on payloads that state nothing, and it skips 'checker 25' (an id, not a count) and disabled jobs |
